message.reasoning:
I am ready to play Monopoly.

I sold Pennsylvania Avenue to player 1 for $200. I now have $235 cash and own VENTNOR_AVENUE, while ATLANTIC_AVENUE and MARVIN_GARDENS remain mortgaged.

I am deciding on post-turn actions. I have $235 cash and no mortgaged properties. I am checking the threats from rolling at ATLANTIC_AVENUE.

Rolling from Atlantic Avenue: most spaces are harmless. The Short Line is the main threat, as player 2 owns all four railroads and charges $200. The Luxury Tax costs $100.

Rolling 9 from Atlantic Avenue lands on Short Line, costing $200. Rolling 12 hits the Luxury Tax for $100. Both are affordable with $235 cash.

Roll 6 lands on unowned North Carolina, which costs $300 and is beyond my budget. I will skip it. Roll 4 sends me to Jail without payment. Community Chest and Chance are too variable to assess.

Unmortgaging either property would leave me with too little cash to pay the $200 Short Line rent. I will keep both mortgaged.

I own the full yellow monopoly set but cannot build on mortgaged properties. I am evaluating whether to trade with player 1, who now controls a massive empire of light blues and pinks.

Player 1's empire is split across multiple monopolies. The orange set has hotels on St. James, Tennessee, and New York. The red set is fragmented because Indiana is mortgaged and Illinois belongs to player 2. The green set is incomplete with Pacific mortgaged and North Carolina unowned. The dark blue set is also split since Park Place is mortgaged. Player 1 cannot build on any of these monopolies.

Player 2 owns brown hotels and all four railroads. Player 1 has $814 cash and player 3 is bankrupt. I am the weakest player. I need to unmortgage both yellows and build houses to create a strong monopoly. The total cost is $297. I only have $235.

I will end the turn without spending cash. I cannot afford to unmortgage both yellows or build houses yet. I am now considering trading with player 2.

I rejected trading with player 2. Selling the yellows would end my chances of winning, and getting Illinois would help player 1 more than me. I will end the turn without proposing trades.

I am weighing whether to mortgage Ventnor Avenue for extra cash. I will unmortgage the yellows only if I have a cushion of at least $200 after the next roll.

Mortgaging Ventnor would add $130, but it is my only unmortgaged yellow and the only source of rent. Because the other yellows are mortgaged, I cannot collect the monopoly double-rent bonus on Ventnor. Its base rent is only $22.

I checked the worst-case Chance cards. Boardwalk, Illinois, and St. Charles are all affordable. Boardwalk is owned by player 1 but unrentable because Park Place is mortgaged. Illinois belongs to player 2 and costs only $20. St. Charles is player 1's pink set with no houses. The $130 mortgage cushion is unnecessary.
